bull.t: Strong and growing free cash flow
bull.b: CrowdStrike is converting its subscription growth into substantial cash generation, giving management resources to invest in product development, sales capacity and strategic expansion. Rising free cash flow also strengthens financial resilience and reduces reliance on external funding as the platform scales.

bull.t: Durable recurring growth and customer expansion
bull.b: High recurring ARR growth combined with deeper module adoption supports durable revenue visibility and expansion within existing accounts. Broader platform usage can increase retention, raise customer lifetime value and make CrowdStrike more embedded in enterprise security operations over time.

bull.t: Strong unit economics and improving operating performance
bull.b: Record subscription margins indicate attractive cloud-platform economics and provide room to fund continued innovation while expanding profitability. The sharp increase in operating income suggests operating leverage is emerging, strengthening the earnings potential of future revenue growth.

bear.b: CrowdStrike's accounting profitability has not yet scaled consistently with its expanding revenue and equity base. Negative EBIT and a very thin net margin leave results sensitive to continued investment needs, making durable earnings conversion less proven than its cash-flow performance.

bear.t: Zscaler acquisition faces approval and integration risk
bear.b: The proposed acquisition could expand CrowdStrike's addressable market, but its long approval timeline delays benefits and leaves the strategic outcome uncertain. Regulatory conditions, shareholder approval and eventual platform integration could consume management attention and create execution risk.

bear.t: AI security complexity can delay customer deployment
bear.b: Customer hesitation around shadow AI, agent identities, data access and network destinations can slow adoption of emerging AI-security workloads. Deployment delays may lengthen sales cycles and defer revenue realization, even though the underlying AI security opportunity is strategically attractive.
